prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: ground-only office floor strip for an original native SNES fighting game.
Input images: first image is the edit target, a blank blue-gray floor strip; second image is ONLY the office scene's palette, lighting and pixel-art style reference.
Primary request: redesign the entire first strip as a detailed, attractive warm ochre/tan commercial carpet-tile floor in shallow side-view arcade perspective. Keep its wide horizontal ground-only composition. Clearly readable staggered rectangular tile seams converge gently toward the upper edge. Add restrained woven material grain, small irregular pixel clusters, subtle wear and broad soft cool-blue desk-light shadows. Use about 12 distinct muted tan, warm-brown, cream and blue-gray shades. All detail must survive reduction to approximately 288x40 pixels: chunky intentional early-1990s pixel clusters, visible one-native-pixel seam edges, softly varied tile interiors. The floor should feel illustrated and substantial, not flat squares or smooth gradients.
Constraints: the complete frame is uninterrupted walkable floor, including all edges. No horizon, furniture, desk legs, people, objects, words, numbers, borders, glow, or cast-character shadows. Opaque. Match the office's navy-contour cartoon style while keeping enough mid-tone contrast for dark blue fighter shoes and ground shadows. Do not alter or reproduce the office scenery itself. Retain the first strip's approximately 3:1 width-to-height aspect ratio.

input_roles.role: office palette and illustration style reference

processing: Full authored strip, nearest native conversion to 288x40; native stage encoder assigns six 4bpp stage palettes. No synthetic lines or painted-over texture.
